title: Response cap and visibility policy
framing: The operator publishes its own editorial content (methodology and named-rail measurements) as a publisher, not a hosting platform. It voluntarily mirrors DSA Articles 16, 17, and 20 inside this right-of-reply channel only. UK Defamation Act 2013 s.4 (publication on a matter of public interest) is the primary shield; seeking a subject's comment before publication is part of that defence, not a courtesy.

points.title: One reply per axis per publication
points.text: File separate forms for distinct axes; one revision per axis.

points.title: Length cap
points.text: 500 words for the public reply; 300 words for the quoted passage.

points.title: Visibility timing
points.text: A1, A2, A6, A7, and A8 are pre-moderated before publication. A3, A4, and A5 publish immediately with a 'reply pending review' badge and are confirmed within target.

points.title: Annotate, do not delete
points.text: A disputed claim is retained with strikethrough plus a dated correction note; corrections are logged in a public changelog.

points.title: Six-month complaint window
points.text: From publication or from the last decision by the operator (DSA Article 20(2) analogue).

points.title: Anti-misuse
points.text: Suspension after warning for manifestly unfounded or repeat duplicative replies (DSA Article 23 analogue).

points.title: Human review on every reply
points.text: No fully automated rejection (DSA Article 20(6) analogue).

points.title: Statement of reasons
points.text: Issued whenever a reply is declined, edited, or de-published (DSA Article 17 analogue).

points.title: Rate limit
points.text: Five replies per rail per rolling 30 days, and five per facilitator named in a published result.

points.title: Out-of-court escalation pointer
points.text: To a certified DSA Article 21 out-of-court dispute-settlement body for EU rails; otherwise the UK courts.
